name: dns_blackhole
title: DNS stops answering
description: Total resolver failure. Everything downstream fails too, so the interesting question is whether the agent blames the cause or a symptom.

card.title: The far end is slow to answer
card.summary: Your router and the path out to the internet both look normal, but the services we test are taking 87 ms to send their first byte, about 69 ms more than the network itself explains.
remediation: Check whether other sites are fine; if they are, the problem is at the far end and not with your connection.
Check the service's own status page.
Wait a few minutes; this often clears on its own.

card.title: Your router is slow to respond
card.summary: Round trips to your own router are taking 5 ms with 1 ms of variation. On a healthy home network this is a couple of milliseconds and steady, so something local is loading it up.
remediation: Check whether something on your network is saturating the connection, such as a large upload or a backup.
Power cycle your router: unplug it for 30 seconds, then plug it back in.
Plug in an ethernet cable for anything important in the next few minutes.

evidence.label: mean absolute deviation of gateway RTT within the probe burst

card.title: Name lookups are slow
card.summary: Looking up addresses is taking 46 ms, well above normal for this network. DNS is the internet's phone book: when it is slow, pages feel slow to start even once they load fine.
remediation: Flush the DNS cache on this device.
Try a different DNS resolver in your network settings.
Wait a few minutes; this often clears on its own.
